Downstream impact: [unbraind/pm-cli#1659](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1659), tracked in pm-cli as [pm-usn5k2](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/main/.agents/pm/issues/pm-usn5k2.toon).

## What happened

`test/served-defects.test.ts` spawns an installed pm with `PM_TELEMETRY_SOURCE_CONTEXT: "test"` and `PM_TELEMETRY_INLINE_FLUSH: "1"`. The comment says the intent is to label the runs and to avoid the detached flusher. Under pm-cli's documented policy (docs/CONFIGURATION.md, *Test environments*), a valid explicit `PM_TELEMETRY_SOURCE_CONTEXT` permits intentional test delivery. So the test's expected refusals were sent to the production Sentry project, as `ExtensionCommandError` from `vcs fetch/push/clone/remote` with `pm.error_code=denied`, exit 1, and `environment=test`.

CI runs on 2026-11-04 (00:26–03:45Z, two GitHub runners) created PM-CLI-3R, 3S, 3T, 3V, 3W and 3X. These blocked pm-cli's Auto Release Sentry gate for the 2026.11.4 cut.

## Fix in this repo

For this suite, set `PM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: "1"` (or `DO_NOT_TRACK: "1"`) next to the source-context label, or point the spawned CLI at a local collector. Either way the label stays without delivering to production. pm-cli will separately stop its release gate from counting `environment=test` issues (pm-usn5k2), but test runs should still not reach the production project.

---

### GitHub comments (2)

> **@unbraind** (2026-11-04T10:45:28Z)
>
> Fix in #179 ([pm-vcs-rd82](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-vcs/blob/main/.agents/pm/issues/pm-vcs-rd82.toon)). `testEnvironment()` now adds the hard opt-out `PM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` for every test child, served-defects drops the delivery-permitting label, and a regression test against a local collector proves that a labelled child reports telemetry disabled and sends zero requests. It fails when the opt-out is removed. A project `telemetry.endpoint` is silently ignored, which made "point such tests at a local collector" impossible without editing the global profile by hand. That is reported upstream as unbraind/pm-cli#1660.

> **@unbraind** (2026-11-04T18:38:42Z)
>
> Requirement update, from the fix in #179: the second point above, "keep the test source-context label while preventing delivery to production", is superseded.
> 
> In pm-cli a valid `PM_TELEMETRY_SOURCE_CONTEXT=test` is what permits test delivery, even under `NODE_ENV=test`. Keeping it in children that must never deliver would leave one guard instead of two.
> 
> #179 therefore:
> 
> - hard-disables telemetry and Sentry in every test child (`PM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` in `testEnvironment()`);
> - drops the label from served-defects.
> 
> A regression test shows that a child that *does* carry the label still reports telemetry disabled and sends zero requests. Tracker: pm-vcs-rd82, whose acceptance criteria record the same.
>
served-defects test delivers its expected refusals to production Sentry and blocked the pm-cli daily release
